annotations.annotation_text: Fraternal archetype "CHUFF" on page 220 ("The Mime of Mick, Nick and the Maggies"): the opposing sons — Shem the Penman (introvert artist, tree, darkness) and Shaun the Post (extrovert politician, stone, light) — manifest here within the children's games and pantomime on the green, Chuff vs. Glugg, the twenty-eight Rainbow Girls, the Angelus bell. Their Brunonian dialectic of coinciding opposites propels the chapter's conflict during this Age of Heroes phase.
sources: Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe
Norris, Margot. The Decentered Universe of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/decentereduniver0000norr
Gordon, John. Finnegans Wake: A Plot Summary. https://johngordonfinnegan.weebly.com

annotations.annotation_text: Egyptian eschatology "set" on page 220 ("The Mime of Mick, Nick and the Maggies"): within the children's games and pantomime on the green, Chuff vs. Glugg, the twenty-eight Rainbow Girls, the Angelus bell, HCE appears as the dismembered Osiris and ALP as Isis gathering his scattered limbs. Mark Troy's research traces how Joyce embedded the Papyrus of Ani's resurrection liturgy throughout this Age of Heroes passage — the dream-journey through the underworld (Tuat) toward solar rebirth.
sources: Budge, E.A. Wallis. The Book of the Dead (Papyrus of Ani). https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/1300
Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish
Troy, Mark L. Mummeries of Resurrection. http://www.rosenlake.net
